FINDINGS: Between May 1, 2019 and Jan 13, 2026, 1045 patients were eligible for enrolment. The trial was stopped early for futility and slow enrolment after 424 of 600 planned patients were recruited. 126 patients were randomly assigned to the supine and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 130 to the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 90 to the supine and HFOV group, and 78 to the prone and HFOV group. Median age was 3·3 years (IQR 1·1-10·1), 211 (50%) patients were female, and 213 (50%) were male. There were no significant differences in ventilator-free days between prone and supine positioning (median 17·9 days [IQR 8·9-21·3] vs 17·4 days [6·4-21·9]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for ventilation 0·0 [95% CI -0·8 to 1·0]) or between HFOV and conventional mechanical ventilation (17·3 [5·7-21·6] vs 18·0 [9·9-21·5]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for positioning -0·3 [95% CI -1·5 to 0·5]). 41 (10%) patients had died at day 28, without group differences. Plugging or obstruction of the artificial airway occurred more frequently with prone than supine positioning (14 events in 12 [6%] of 188 patients vs three events in three [2%] of 197 patients; 0·74 [95% CI 0·44-1·26] vs 0·15 [0·05-0·47] events per 100 artificial airway days; rate ratio 4·83 [95% CI 1·38-16·82]). Stage 2 or worse immobility-related pressure injuries also occurred more frequently with prone versus supine positioning (12 [6%] vs two [1%]; relative risk 6·13 [95% CI 1·45-25·97]). Haemodynamic instability occurred more frequently with HFOV than conventional mechanical ventilation (41 events in 19 [13%] of 141 patients vs 38 events in 22 [9%] of 244 patients; 2·21 [95% CI 1·63-3·00] vs 1·22 [0·89-1·68] events per 100 paediatric intensive care unit days; rate ratio 1·84 [95% CI 1·18-2·87]). One serious adverse event, an unwitnessed self-extubation followed by cardiopulmonary arrest, occurred in a patient in the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group. INTERPRETATION: We found no evidence to support prone positioning or HFOV as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. Thus, the routine use of these strategies in this population is not recommended. FUNDING: US National Institutes of Health/National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

title: Interpreting High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin in Clinical Practice and Emerging Directions: Detection Is No Longer Diagnosis.
abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have solved the problem of detecting myocardial injury and, in doing so, created the problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are now known to be common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease, and the central challenge of contemporary practice is no longer whether myocardial injury can be detected, but whether it can be correctly classified. Misclassification occurs in both directions and with real consequence: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary myocardial infarction (MI), contributing to the overdiagnosis of MI, and chronic myocardial injury, which carries a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. This narrative review argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and instead requires integrated, context-aware interpretation grounded in 4 domains: 1) the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results; 2) the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the European Society of Cardiology 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support; 3) rigorous application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis, and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification; and 4) recognition of the non-acute coronary syndrome conditions-chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome, and others-in which troponin elevation is expected rather than anomalous. We provide explicit bedside guidance for the situations that clinicians find most difficult, including suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. Finally, we review emerging understanding of troponin biology, clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin, which may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden. Until then, that burden rests with the clinician.

title: Effects of Walnut Consumption on Anti-MDA-LDL Antibodies and Immunoglobulins in the WAHA Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Higher total serum IgG levels have been associated with protection from cardiovascular events in ASCOT (Anglo-Scandinavian Cardiac Outcomes Trial). Antibodies against oxidized low-density lipoprotein (LDL) have also been linked to favorable clinical and vascular imaging outcomes. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to determine whether regular walnut consumption influences circulating immunoglobulins, malondialdehyde-modified LDL (MDA-LDL), a highly immunogenic form of oxidized LDL, and antibodies against MDA-LDL. METHODS: The Walnuts and Healthy Aging study was a two-center, randomized controlled trial conducted in Spain and the United States. Adults aged 63 to 79 years were assigned to a walnut-enriched diet or a control diet excluding walnuts for 2 years. Serum total immunoglobulin G (IgG), total immunoglobulin M (IgM), MDA-LDL, and IgG and IgM anti MDA-LDL antibodies were measured by enzyme-linked immunoassays in 474 participants. RESULTS: Baseline immunoglobulin concentrations differed substantially by study center. Participants from the United States had 25% lower total IgM and IgG concentrations than participants from Spain. Walnut consumption increased total serum IgG by 11% in the U.S. cohort (95% CI: 0%-24%; P = 0.040), whereas pooled analysis showed a 6% increase across both cohorts (95% CI: 0%-12%; P = 0.041). Over the 2-year study period, total IgM and both IgG and IgM anti-MDA-LDL concentrations declined significantly in both the control and intervention groups. CONCLUSIONS: Long-term walnut consumption was associated with a modest increase in total serum IgG but had no significant effect on total IgM, MDA-LDL, or antibodies against MDA-LDL. Baseline IgG and IgM concentrations were substantially lower among U.S. participants, suggesting that geographic, environmental, social, or genetic factors may modulate immune biomarkers independently of dietary intervention.

title: T-Cell-Derived IFNγ Instructs ECM Crosslinking by Cardiac Fibroblasts Through LOXL3 in Experimental Cardiometabolic HFpEF.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a major clinical challenge characterized by diastolic dysfunction. Left ventricular stiffening and inflammation are hallmarks of HFpEF, yet the contribution of ECM (extracellular matrix) stiffness and the immune-stromal mechanisms driving ECM stiffening in cardiometabolic HFpEF remain poorly understood. METHODS: We used the murine 2-hit model of cardiometabolic HFpEF, in which the combination of high-fat diet and hypertension induced by L-nitro-arginine-methyl ester causes diastolic dysfunction. We evaluated diastolic function by echocardiography and ECM mechanics by uniaxial tensile testing of decellularized cardiac tissue. Functional in vivo studies included genetic depletion of T cells, IFNγ (interferon-γ) knockout mice, and pharmacological lysyl oxidase inhibition. We combined cocultures of CD4+ T cells and cardiac fibroblasts with mechanical testing of cardiac ECM and molecular biology to elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Left ventricular ECM stiffness strongly correlated with impaired diastolic function in experimental cardiometabolic HFpEF. Cardiac CD4+ T-cell infiltration was required for ECM stiffening and upregulation of lysyl oxidase enzymes in cardiac fibroblast. We discovered that CD4+ T-cell-derived IFNγ was required to induce LOXL3 in cardiac fibroblast, which increased ECM stiffness in vitro. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that a signaling axis involving IFNγ, PI3K (phosphoinositide 3-kinase), AKT, and HIF1α (hypoxia-inducible factor-1α) drives LOXL3 expression and subsequent collagen crosslinking. Genetic or pharmacological disruption of this IFNγ-HIF1α-LOXL3 axis attenuated adverse ECM remodeling and improved diastolic function. CONCLUSIONS: CD4+ T cells promote pathological ECM stiffening in cardiometabolic HFpEF through IFNγ-mediated, cardiac fibroblast LOXL3-dependent ECM crosslinking. Targeting this immune-stromal pathway may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for HFpEF.

title: Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials.
abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.

title: Intersection of Patient and Hospital Rurality in Heart Failure Care and Outcomes.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Rural-urban disparities in heart failure (HF) care delivery and outcomes are well documented. However, it remains unclear if differences in outcomes after HF hospitalization are primarily driven by patient rural residence, hospital resources, or both. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of patient and hospital rurality with quality of care and postdischarge outcomes after hospitalization for HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries in US hospitals with HFrEF with an index hospitalization from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2021. Included were Medicare beneficiaries discharged alive after an index hospitalization for HFrEF. Participants were classified as rural patients hospitalized in rural hospitals (rural-rural), rural patients in urban hospitals (rural-urban), urban patients in urban hospitals (urban-urban), and urban patients in rural hospitals (urban-rural). Study data were analyzed from July to September 2026. EXPOSURES: Patient rural residence and hospital rurality. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality after hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included inpatient cardiology consultation, 90-day postdischarge guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) use based on prescription fills, and HF readmission at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year. RESULTS: Among 735 460 beneficiaries (median [IQR] age, 77 [70-85] years; 415 077 male [56.4%]), 69 061 (9.4%) were rural-rural, 65 510 (8.9%) rural-urban, 582 947 (79.3%) urban-urban, and 17 942 (2.4%) urban-rural. Compared with rural patients treated in rural hospitals, rural patients treated in urban hospitals were more likely to receive inpatient cardiology consultation (odds ratio [OR], 2.02; 95% CI, 1.84-2.22) and initiation of several GDMT classes, including β-blockers (OR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.16-1.25), ARNIs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.13-1.34), MRAs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.15-1.31), and SGLT2Is (OR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.32-1.67). They also had lower rates of HF readmission and mortality at all time points (HF readmission 1-year: OR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.88; mortality 1-year: OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.89-0.94) than rural-rural patients. Compared with urban patients hospitalized at urban hospitals, rural patients hospitalized at urban hospitals more often received inpatient cardiology consultation (OR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.31-1.44), whereas postdischarge GDMT differences were modest (absolute difference in GDMT score 0.09 points; 95% CI, 0.05-0.14). Rural patients also had lower HF readmission (1-year OR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.79-0.82) but higher 30- and 90-day mortality than urban patients (30-day OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; 90-day OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.08). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results suggest that hospital rurality was associated with lower odds of GDMT use and higher rates of all-cause mortality, whereas rural residence was associated with mortality differences despite treatment in urban hospitals. Interventions addressing both inpatient resource disparities and postdischarge transitions of care may reduce rural-urban inequities in HF outcomes.

title: Norepinephrine Equivalent Dose for Mortality Risk Stratification in VA-ECMO Cardiogenic Shock.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) complicated by vasoplegia requiring venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) often need escalating vasopressor support and face high mortality. Norepinephrine equivalent dose (NEE) quantifies vasopressor burden, yet its prognostic value in VA-ECMO remains undefined. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to characterize the dose-response relationship between NEE and 30-day mortality, identify a clinically relevant NEE threshold, and determine factors associated with high vasopressor burden. METHODS: This bicentric retrospective study included 572 consecutive patients with CS requiring VA-ECMO. We collected vasopressor regimens, NEE trajectories, and hemodynamic parameters at predefined intervals. Restricted cubic splines assessed dose-response linearity. Maximally selected rank statistics with bootstrap validation identified optimal thresholds. Cox models estimated mortality risk. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with high vasopressor burden. RESULTS: The median NEE at ECMO initiation was 0.30 (IQR: 0.09-0.72) μg·kg-1·min-1; 86.2% received norepinephrine. NEE showed a linear dose-response with mortality (HR: 1.06 per 0.1 μg·kg-1·min-1 increment; 95% CI: 1.04-1.08; P < 0.001). A threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 identified high vasopressor burden with elevated 30-day mortality (61.8% vs 42.6%; P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 1.42; 95% CI: 1.11-1.81; P = 0.005). Factors associated with high vasopressor burden included mechanical ventilation (OR: 2.96; 95% CI: 1.08-8.07), prior epinephrine use (OR: 1.87; 95% CI: 1.12-3.14), renal replacement therapy before VA-ECMO (OR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.02-3.03), baseline lactate (OR: 1.05 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 1.01-1.09), and lower Survival After Veno-Arterial ECMO score (OR: 0.96 per point; 95% CI: 0.92-1.00). Left ventricular unloading was inversely associated (OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.34-0.87). CONCLUSIONS: In VA-ECMO-supported CS with vasoplegia, vasopressor burden shows a linear relationship with mortality. A NEE threshold of 0.443 μg·kg-1·min-1 may identify patients with elevated mortality risk.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year. RESULTS: We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; P=0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04864145.

title: Glutaminolysis Shapes Cardiac Resilience to Stress via Mitochondrial Glutathione.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac reserve is a strong predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that enable the heart to mount an adaptive response to stress remain poorly understood. In this study, we sought to dissect the specific role of glutaminolysis, a key anaplerotic and redox-supporting pathway, in regulating cardiac reserve. METHODS: Cardiac reserve was assessed by echocardiography under β-adrenergic stimulation in mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase and in wild-type controls. Stable isotope tracing with [U-13C] glutamine was performed in Langendorff-perfused hearts. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of acute glutamine supplementation in healthy volunteers was conducted to evaluate translational relevance (ChiCTR2400082676). RESULTS: During acute stress, such as exercise or β-adrenergic stimulation, glutaminolysis was rapidly mobilized to supply mitochondrial glutathione, preserving mitochondrial redox homeostasis and sustaining cardiac contractile reserve. Mice with cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of glutaminase exhibited marked impairments in both contractile reserve and exercise capacity, accompanied by a failure to elevate mitochondrial glutathione and consequent mitochondrial oxidative stress. Chronic exercise training upregulated cardiac glutaminase expression and expanded the mitochondrial glutathione pool, linking this adaptive mechanism to training-induced improvements in cardiac reserve. In humans, acute oral glutamine supplementation enhanced cardiac reserve, as assessed by exercise stress echocardiography, in a placebo-controlled crossover design. CONCLUSIONS: These findings reveal a novel metabolic paradigm in which glutaminolysis functions as a dynamic pathway supporting mitochondrial health and cardiac resilience, and highlight glutamine supplementation as a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance cardiac reserve.

title: BAHCC1 Drives Smooth Muscle Plasticity and Neointima via Epigenetic Repression.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotypic plasticity drives neointimal hyperplasia (IH) and contributes to atherosclerosis. Epigenetic mechanisms have been implicated in SMC plasticity, but the roles of epigenetic reader proteins are poorly understood. BAHCC1 (bromo adjacent homology domain coiled-coil 1) is a newly identified reader of the gene-repression histone mark histone-3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3). Its role in vascular remodeling is unknown. METHODS: We investigated BAHCC1 in human restenotic and atherosclerotic arteries and in rat and mouse arterial injury models using BAHCC1 silencing, SMC-specific deletion, and an H3K27me3-binding-deficient knock-in mutation. Mechanistic studies in human aortic SMCs integrated transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling, protein-interaction assays, and single-guide RNA-dCas9-based epigenetic editing. RESULTS: BAHCC1 was upregulated in human restenotic and atherosclerotic arteries and rat arteries with IH. While BAHCC1 silenc ing reduced IH in balloon-injured rat arteries, SMC-specific BAHCC1 deletion and the H3K27me3-binding-deficient mutation (BAHCC1Y2537A) attenuated IH in wire-injured mouse arteries. In human SMCs, mitogen induced BAHCC1 expression through nuclear factor Y subunit-α, promoting BAHCC1-dependent dedifferentiation. Integrated transcriptomics and epigenomics identified LMO7 (LIM domain only 7), an IH suppressor, as a key BAHCC1-repressed target. BAHCC1 occupancy at LMO7 required BAHCC1-H3K27me3 interaction, and LMO7-targeted H3K27me3 enrichment through epigenetic editing repressed its expression in a BAHCC1-dependent manner. Furthermore, BAHCC1 associated with SAP30 and RBBP4/7 to form a corepressor complex. Functionally, LMO7 silencing reversed the effects of BAHCC1 knockdown on human SMC phenotype and exacerbated IH in BAHCC1Y2537A mice. Human genetic analyses further identified BAHCC1 variants associated with cardiovascular phenotypes and BAHCC1 expression. CONCLUSIONS: BAHCC1 is a previously unrecognized epigenetic driver of vascular remodeling. By reading H3K27me3 and recruiting corepressors to repress gene expression, BAHCC1 promotes pathological SMC phenotypic transition and IH, highlighting the BAHCC1 pathway as a potential therapeutic target for IH-associated vascular disease.

title: Vascular Brain Injury in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at higher risk of vascular brain lesions. Whether AF and HF synergistically amplify this risk is unclear. In this study, we explored the association of HF and AF and their interaction with the prevalence of MRI-detected vascular brain lesions. METHODS: We analysed 2,712 participants from the Swiss-AF study who underwent standardized brain-MRI and categorised them based on their AF diagnosis and history of HF. In the brain-MRI, we assessed large non-cortical and cortical infarcts (LNCCI), small non-cortical infarcts (SNCI) and white matter hyperintensities (WMH). Logistic regression models were used to analyse associations between AF, HF and their interaction with vascular brain lesions, adjusting for pre-selected covariates. RESULTS: Mean age was 73 years and 30.8% were female. The prevalence of ischemic brain infarcts and WMH increased across groups defined by AF and HF status (brain infarcts: AF-/HF- 22.8%, AF-/HF+ 30.2%, AF+/HF- 34.6%, AF+/HF+ 44.6%; WMH: AF-/HF- 43.2% AF-/HF+ 49.7%, AF+/HF- 50.4%, AF+/HF+ 65.6%). No significant interaction between AF and HF was observed for any brain lesion subtype. Both AF and HF (OR, 95% CI, p-value) were independently associated with brain infarcts (AF: 1.78, 1.48-2.16, p<0.001; HF: 1.32, 1.06-1.64, p<0.001) and WMH (AF: 1.71, 1.44-2.03, p<0.001; HF: 1.45, 1.17-1.80, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: AF and HF are independently associated with a higher prevalence of ischemic brain lesions, with the greatest burden observed in patients with both conditions. No interaction was found between AF and HF with regards to vascular brain lesions.

title: Association Between Cardiologist Ambulatory Workload and Evidence-Based Therapy for Heart Failure.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Most eligible patients are not prescribed guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF). Increased time pressures for providers in the ambulatory setting may contribute to these shortfalls. We assessed the association between cardiologist ambulatory workload and guideline-directed medical therapy prescription for patients with heart failure with reduced EF. METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study of patients with heart failure with reduced EF (EF ≤40%) seen by a cardiologist from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, using deidentified administrative and electronic health record data from Optum Labs Data Warehouse, which includes data from multiple health systems across the United States. The primary exposure was ambulatory workload, measured as the average number of visits per day, categorized into quartiles. The primary outcome was "comprehensive quadruple therapy," defined as prescription for all 4 guideline-directed medical therapies: β-blocker; angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor; mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor. Analyses were conducted using generalized estimating equations, adjusted for demographic and clinical variables. RESULTS: Overall, 40 173 patients were seen by 881 cardiologists (median ambulatory workload, 9.1 patients per day; interquartile range=5.1-13.0). The percentage of patients prescribed comprehensive quadruple therapy was higher among patients in lower quartiles (quartile 1: 14%; quartile 2: 9.7%; quartile 3: 8.9%; quartile 4: 7.4%; P<0.001). In adjusted analysis, there was a graded association between lower workload quartile and higher odds of comprehensive quadruple therapy, compared with the highest quartile (odds ratio [95% CI], P value=quartile 1: 1.35 [1.09-1.66], 0.008; quartile 2: 1.20 [1.00-1.43], 0.050; quartile 3: 1.11 [0.93-1.32], 0.28; quartile 4 [reference]). CONCLUSIONS: Seeing a cardiologist with lower ambulatory workload was associated with increased prescribing of guideline-recommended, life-saving therapy in patients with heart failure with reduced EF. Current models that incentivize more visits per day may negatively impact care in the ambulatory setting.

title: Clinical Impact of Multiple-Clip Implantation for Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Residual moderate or greater mitral regurgitation (MR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the prognostic impact of implanting additional clips in patients with significant residual MR after the first clip remains uncertain. We evaluated the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of multiple-clip implantation for significant residual MR following placement of the initial clip. METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 826 patients with moderate or greater residual MR on intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiography after placement of the first clip during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center from 2014 to 2023. Patients were categorized into single-clip (n=113) and multiple-clip (n=713) groups. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year. RESULTS: Procedural technical success and complication rates were comparable between groups. The multiple-clip group demonstrated greater MR reduction and higher transmitral pressure gradients at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. At 1 year, the composite end point occurred less frequently in the multiple-clip group than in the single-clip group (16.8% versus 29.2%; P=0.002), along with greater and more sustained improvement in New York Heart Association functional class. In subgroup analyses, multiple-clip implantation consistently reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with moderate as well as moderate-severe/severe residual MR. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with significant residual MR after implanting the first clip, multiple-clip implantation improved MR reduction and 1-year outcomes without increasing complications. Even in moderate residual MR, additional clips were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes.

title: Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women's Cardiovascular Care: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
abstract: Improving cardiovascular health in women is an urgent public health priority given the persistent and pervasive gaps in awareness, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease in this population. Advances in scientific understanding have led to increased recognition of female-specific considerations in cardiovascular disease, which informed the development of the Female Life Stage construct by the American Heart Association in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. This construct integrates assessment of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across life stages. However, gaps remain in operationalizing this construct and optimizing the delivery of patient-centered, interdisciplinary care among women. Over the past several decades, women's cardiovascular centers have emerged as leaders, expanded rapidly, and elevated the recognition of cardiovascular diseases that exclusively, disproportionately, or differently affect women (eg, myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, Takotsubo syndrome). In this science advisory, we describe the current landscape of women's cardiovascular centers and propose a national infrastructure to support the expansion of dedicated Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women's Cardiovascular Care. These centers are conceptualized as interdisciplinary care models comprising 4 defining pillars: interdisciplinary clinical care, education and training, research, and community engagement. By establishing integrated pathways that span clinical disciplines, these centers can reduce fragmentation, enhance earlier risk identification, and expand opportunities to increase representation of women in clinical research. In doing so, they offer a bold opportunity for a scalable and equitable model to improve cardiovascular health for all women.

title: Right Atrial Phasic Function Improves CMR-Based Prognostication in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: AIMS: In multiple cardiovascular diseases, right atrial (RA) function can serve as an independent predictor for the clinical status and prognosis. However, the prognostic value of RA strain in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) remains considerably unknown. This study aims to explore the relationships between RA strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging-feature tracking (CMR-FT) and adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF. METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with HFmrEF who were referred for echocardiography and CMR at two tertiary medical centers from April 2016 to September 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF-related hospitalization and cardiac transplantation. The findings were validated in a cohort of patients with HFmrEF enrolled from two additional tertiary care centers (January 2019 to January 2025). The development cohort included 1317 patients, and the validation cohort comprised 385 patients. During a median follow-up period of 2.8 years and 2.1 years, respectively, 243 and 72 patients in the development cohort and validation cohort reached the primary endpoint, respectively. Cox regression analysis showed that RA conduit strain was an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR: 0.86 [0.82, 0.90]; P < .001). The full model integrating clinical variables, traditional imaging, and RA strain achieved the best predictive performance (C-index: 0.80 in development, 0.81 in validation cohorts). CONCLUSION: RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​.

title: Outcomes of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome by Subtype and Presence of Ventriculocoronary Connections: A Fetal Heart Society Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is classified by anatomic subtype: mitral atresia and aortic atresia (MA/AA), mitral stenosis and aortic atresia (MS/AA), and mitral stenosis and aortic stenosis (MS/AS). The MS/AA subtype is associated with ventriculocoronary connections (VCCs). We assessed whether specific HLHS subtypes are associated with an increased risk of mortality and whether this risk is stratified by VCCs identified during fetal or postnatal echocardiography. We also assessed whether the type of neonatal intervention performed modified the risk. METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective cohort study of fetuses and infants <2 months old with HLHS who were admitted between January 2012 and December 2016 to participating Fetal Heart Society institutions. Clinical and demographic data were collected. Fetal and transthoracic echocardiograms from a subset of patients with MS/AA and those with suspected VCCs were reviewed. Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed, controlling for cardiac center (random effect), birth weight, genetic diagnosis, extracardiac malformation, and restricted/intact atrial septum. RESULTS: Among 16 centers, 591 patients were born alive with intention to treat. MA/AA was the most common subtype (261, 44%), followed by MS/AA (200, 34%) and MS/AS (130, 22%). Of those with MS/AA, 115 (58%) had suspected VCCs. Median follow-up was 9.0 (interquartile range: 7.0, 10.8) years. Overall transplant-free survival (TFS) was 55.6% at 5 years and 49.4% at 10 years. When comparing MA/AA, MS/AS, and MS/AA with and without VCCs (reference group: MS/AA without VCCs), MS/AA with VCCs had the lowest TFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.69 [1.12, 2.57]; 5-year TFS, 44.7%; 10-year TFS, 40.3%). This was followed by MA/AA (HR, 1.40 [0.95, 2.05]; 5-year TFS, 54.1%; 10-year TFS, 46.6%). Survival of MS/AA without VCCs (5-year TFS, 60.4%; 10-year TFS, 56.9%) was similar to MS/AS (HR, 0.91 [0.59, 1.41]; 5-year TFS, 65.0%; 10-year TFS, 58.3%). Among those with a prenatal diagnosis of HLHS (n=532), patients with MS/AA and VCCs suspected on fetal echocardiogram had a lower TFS compared with those with MS/AA without fetal suspicion for VCCs (HR, 1.79 [1.12, 2.85]). Fetal echocardiography was used to diagnose VCCs in 33 of 103 (32%) cases with MS/AA and VCCs suspected postnatally. Of patients with MS/AA and VCCs, type of stage I palliation was not associated with TFS (P=0.784). CONCLUSIONS: In a large, multicenter cohort of HLHS patients, the MS/AA subtype with VCCs had the lowest TFS. Prenatal diagnosis of VCCs was associated with a lower TFS. This study underscores the prognostic value of assessing for VCCs in patients with HLHS both before and after birth.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Automated Optical Coherence Tomography Analysis for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Planning: From Plaque Analysis to Precision Lesion Preparation and Stent Optimization.
abstract: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains the cornerstone of revascularization in coronary artery disease. However, despite advances in stent technology, adverse outcomes related to suboptimal stent placement including under-expansion, malapposition, incomplete coverage, edge dissection, and neoatherosclerosis persist. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is the highest resolution widely available intravascular imaging modality, allowing unparalleled visualization of stent-vessel interactions and plaque morphology. However, there are significant barriers to large-scale OCT adoption, including time-consuming manual interpretation and dependence on the operator, resulting in significant variability between analysts. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based automated OCT analysis promises to assist PCI by delivering rapid, reproducible, and standardized stent optimization, but current analysis systems lack important features to optimize stent placement. This review summarizes the principles of OCT in PCI, the evidence for OCT-guided optimization, and recent advances in AI-driven automated OCT analysis. We discuss plaque analysis and classification, highlighting how AI-driven automated OCT analysis can identify fibrous, lipid-rich, and calcified lesions and guide tailored lesion preparation using balloons, specialty balloons, drug-coated balloons, intravascular lithotripsy, and atherectomy. We outline emerging AI-enabled workflows for fully automated PCI optimization, evaluate clinical outcomes, interpretability, and workflow integration. Finally, we explore future directions including AI imaging-physiology fusion, multiomics integration, and robotics. If successful, automated AI-empowered OCT analysis could become a central imaging platform for precision PCI, enabling tailored lesion preparation, optimal stent deployment, and improved clinical outcomes in coronary artery disease management.

title: Impact of obesity on clinical outcomes and the treatment effect of catheter ablation in atrial fibrillation: insights from CABANA.
abstract: AIMS: Obesity and atrial fibrillation (AF) are global epidemics, often co-existing and compounding cardiovascular risk. While catheter ablation has emerged as an effective strategy for rhythm control in symptomatic AF, it remains unclear whether obesity modifies its benefit. This post hoc analysis of the CABANA trial investigates the influence of baseline obesity on clinical outcomes after catheter ablation vs. drug therapy in AF patients. METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 2170 CABANA participants with available body mass index (BMI) were included. Obesity was defined by BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2, and Class II obesity by BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2. Adverse outcomes, AF recurrence, and functional status were analysed using Cox, mixed-effects, and generalized estimating equation models, assessing treatment-by-obesity interactions. Obese patients exhibited higher comorbidity burden, worse baseline functional status, and more persistent AF compared to non-obese counterparts. Higher BMI was associated with increased cardiovascular hospitalization and a higher New York Heart Association functional class. Catheter ablation significantly reduced the risk of AF recurrence and improved symptom burden and functional capacity, irrespective of obesity status. No significant interaction was found between BMI and treatment effect on the primary composite endpoint of cardiovascular hospitalization or all-cause mortality. However, patients with Class II obesity or higher had worse absolute outcomes despite similar relative benefits from ablation. CONCLUSION: While obesity is associated with worse baseline status and outcomes, it was not shown to significantly alter the relative effectiveness of AF ablation compared to drug therapy. These findings support a multifaceted approach integrating rhythm control with upstream interventions targeting obesity-related atrial remodelling and comorbidity management.

title: Complementary Cardiohepatic Prognostic Value of Hepatic Steatosis in Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic steatosis carries substantial cardiovascular risk, whereas cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome contributes to liver disease progression, highlighting the need for integrated cardiohepatic risk assessment. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate whether hepatic steatosis provides incremental prognostic value beyond CKM staging for cardiovascular and liver outcomes. METHODS: We included 313,970 UK Biobank participants with CKM stages 0 to 3. Hepatic steatosis was primarily assessed using the Fatty Liver Index, with the Hepatic Steatosis Index as an alternative measure and the Fibrosis-4 Index for liver fibrosis. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). The secondary outcome was major adverse liver events (MALEs). RESULTS: During a median 15.7-year follow-up, 32,110 MACEs and 1,599 MALEs occurred. Hepatic steatosis and advanced CKM were independently associated with both outcomes, with coexistence conferring the highest risks (MACEs: HR: 2.33; 95% CI: 2.19-2.47; MALEs: HR: 5.09; 95% CI: 3.97-6.54, vs neither exposure). For MACEs, the association with hepatic steatosis was stronger in nonadvanced CKM (stages 0-2: HR: 1.51; 95% CI: 1.48-1.55) than in stage 3 (HR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.97-1.23; Pinteraction < 0.001). For MALEs, hepatic steatosis mediated 41.1% of the association with CKM stage. The findings were consistent across alternative steatosis measures, whereas liver fibrosis showed no significant stage-dependent association with MACEs and a smaller mediation proportion for MALEs. Adding hepatic steatosis to CKM staging improved discrimination for both outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Hepatic steatosis provided complementary cardiovascular and liver prognostic value beyond CKM staging, supporting its integration for more comprehensive cardiohepatic risk stratification.

title: CCR2-Dependent Myeloid Cell Recruitment Links Post-MI Heart Failure to Pulmonary Hypertension.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease (PH-LHD) is a common complication of myocardial infarction (MI) and heart failure (HF). Myeloid inflammation is a major hallmark of both the local cardiac and systemic post-MI response, with resident and recruited monocyte-derived macrophages orchestrating each step of the ensuing inflammatory cascade, from clearance of dead cardiomyocytes to scar tissue formation. Similarly, myeloid inflammation is a key feature of the PH lung, driving remodeling of small pulmonary vessels. We thus hypothesized that MI-induced systemic myeloid inflammation contributes directly to the development of PH-LHD. METHODS: We assessed expression of inflammatory adhesion molecules, as markers of vascular inflammatory activation and myeloid cell recruitment pathways, in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, PH-LHD, as well as in a PH-LHD rat model. We then induced MI and subsequent HF in 8- to 10-week-old female C57BL/6J mice via permanent ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. HF mice were then treated with a CCR2 (C-C chemokine receptor 2) antagonist to block monocyte recruitment and the development of PH-LHD was assessed at 6 weeks post-MI by a combination of invasive hemodynamics, flow cytometry, echocardiography, and lung histology. RESULTS: Expression of key inflammatory adhesion molecules, including VCAM1 and SELE, was increased in PH-LHD lungs from humans and rats. Following early post-MI development of HF with reduced ejection fraction, mice exhibited increased numbers of circulating monocytes, lung monocytes, and lung interstitial macrophages, as well as PH-LHD by 6 weeks, characterized by right ventricular hypertrophy, elevated right ventricular pressures, and lung vascular remodeling of small-to-medium-sized pulmonary vessels. Administration of the selective CCR2 antagonist RS102895 from day 10 post-MI to reduce monocyte tissue recruitment attenuated lung vascular remodeling, right ventricular systolic and diastolic pressures, right ventricular hypertrophy, and lung adhesion molecule expression at 6 weeks, compared with vehicle-treated controls, without improving the underlying left-sided HF. CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates a causal role for CCR2-dependent myeloid cell recruitment in the progression from MI-induced HF to secondary pulmonary vascular disease.

title: Using rare coding variants in SLC5A2 to explore the impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on cardiorenal outcomes.
abstract: AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are agents originally developed as glucose-lowering drugs but now widely used to improve cardiorenal outcomes, including in patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease regardless of diabetes status. However, their exact mode of action remains unclear. Here, we investigated the association of loss-of-function (LoF) and other rare coding variants in the SLC5A2 gene, as a genetic model of altered SGLT2 function, with 13 cardiometabolic and renal traits and clinical outcomes. METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 442 570 European ancestry participants from the UK Biobank with exome sequence and phenotype data were included. We applied SAIGE-GENE+ for gene-based and single-variant association tests in the full study population and in individuals with heart failure, renal failure, and type 2 diabetes (T2D). A total of 52 LoF variants in SLC5A2 were identified. Rare variants in SLC5A2 were associated with decreased uric acid (PCauchy = 4.98 × 10-13) and with increased haematocrit (PCauchy = 1.67 × 10-5), haemoglobin (PCauchy = 1.60 × 10-5), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (PCauchy = 9.88 × 10-4). One frameshift variant (rs267607067) was significantly associated with increased haemoglobin (β = 0.33 [95% CI 0.15-0.51]; P-value = 2.40 × 10-4) and another (rs768095044) with decreased uric acid (β = -0.31 [95% CI -0.49 to -0.13]; P-value = 4.22 × 10-4). In patients with T2D, the rare variants within SLC5A2 were also associated with a lower probability of having heart failure (PCauchy = 4.00 × 10-4). CONCLUSION: Rare genetic variants in SLC5A2 were associated with increased haemoglobin and decreased uric acid. These variants were also associated with a lower probability of heart failure among participants with T2D, providing tentative genetic support for a cardioprotective effect of SGLT2 inhibition.

title: Safety and Effectiveness of a Novel Laser-Based Intravascular Lithotripsy System for Coronary Calcium: FRACTURE Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a promising option to modify calcium. OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a novel laser- and optic-based quad-emitter IVL system in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. METHODS: FRACTURE was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiac events (MACE; composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success (successful stent delivery with a final residual stenosis <50% and freedom from in-hospital MACE). Both endpoints were evaluated against prespecified performance goals. An optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy was performed. RESULTS: A total of 420 patients (mean age: 71.2 ± 9.01 years; 74.0% male) were enrolled. Median calcified length was 34.4 mm (Q1-Q3: 21.3-52.5 mm). Among 106 patients with OCT, at the site of maximum calcification, the calcium arc was 271.89° ± 77.35° and the median thickness was 0.88 mm (Q1-Q3: 0.72-1.11 mm). OCT confirmed calcium fracture in 67% of lesions; the median minimal stent area was 6.51 mm2 (Q1-Q3: 4.85-7.78 mm2), and stent expansion was 94.2% ± 19.4% at the site of maximum calcification. The primary safety endpoint of 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). The primary effectiveness endpoint of procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). CONCLUSIONS: The quad-emitter IVL system is a safe and effective option to modify severe calcified coronary lesions and facilitate stent implantation. REGISTRATION: (Modification of Coronary Calcium With Laser Based Intravascular Lithotripsy for Coronary Artery Disease [FRACTURE]; NCT06181240).

title: Redefining Cardiometabolic Disease: Expert Consensus on the CardioVascular-Kidney-Liver-Metabolic (CVKLM) Multiorgan Staging.
abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases increasingly manifest as interconnected dysfunction across the heart, vasculature, kidneys, liver, and metabolic system. The global rise in obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes, together with therapies benefiting multiple organs, has reshaped the epidemiology and understanding of cardiometabolic disease, exposing the limitations of organ-specific or single-stage approaches. The cardioVascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CVKLM) framework is a multidimensional staging system in which cardiac, vascular, kidney, liver, and metabolic involvement are graded independently from absent to advanced. Analogous to tumour-node-metastasis staging, it provides a standardized language describing disease severity within each organ and its distribution across organs. Rather than replacing existing classifications, CVKLM integrates universal heart failure stages, validated vascular risk assessment, KDIGO chronic kidney disease stratification, contemporary metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and advanced liver disease criteria, and current definitions of diabetes and clinical obesity. Unlike hierarchical frameworks assigning a single overall stage, CVKLM preserves organ-specific information and records coexisting abnormalities across domains. Intended for clinical and research phenotyping and staging rather than as a validated global risk score, it may facilitate systematic recognition of concomitant organ disease, support existing organ-specific diagnostic, referral, and treatment pathways, and provide a standardized taxonomy for observational studies and clinical trials. The prognostic significance of CVKLM profiles, their incremental value beyond established risk tools, and their clinical utility remain to be established. By integrating these domains within a common architecture, CVKLM offers a pragmatic framework spanning the full spectrum of cardiometabolic disease, from preclinical involvement to advanced multiorgan failure.

title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery. METHODS: In this single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound-guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge. RESULTS: A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention-to-treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46-2.15], adjusted P=0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross-clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06-0.80]; adjusted P=0.022), lower postoperative high-sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: -2562 ng/L [95% CI, -4301 to -45]; P=0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06-0.98]; adjusted P=0.046). CONCLUSIONS: While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high-sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn; URL Identifier: ChiCTR2300068572.

title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization. RESULTS: During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall P=0.71; P for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank P=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]). CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

title: Great debate: a dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome.
abstract: Suspected myocardial infarction in patients with acute chest pain at rest is one of the most common diagnostic categories leading to emergency hospital admission and emergency department overcrowding worldwide. Efforts are being made to improve the efficiency of currently used triage and diagnostic work-up strategies. Despite major advances in recent years with the use of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin, challenges still exist regarding how to accurately and rapidly rule out or rule in myocardial infarction, as current strategies are relatively slow due to the need for serial troponin measurements. The 2023 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines recommend a 0 h/1 h or a 0 h/2 h high-sensitivity troponin diagnostic algorithm, instead of the previously suggested 0 h/3 h diagnostic protocol, to reduce the time required to discharge patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome/myocardial infarction. The ESC endorsed algorithms are not without difficulty, and alternative ways of improving triaging have been proposed, particularly a dual biomarker rule-out strategy involving the combined measurement of copeptin and troponin. Supporters of the dual biomarker strategy argue that a timely optimized algorithm can potentially allow the safe rule-out of myocardial infarction earlier than currently used strategies. In the present Great Debate article, two expert teams discuss the 'pros' and 'cons' of implementing single vs dual biomarker strategies for the rule-in and rule-out of myocardial infarction, under the moot topic 'A dual biomarker strategy improves the triage of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome'. They address in detail many of the controversial issues currently affecting everyday clinical practice and provide insightful comments on how to best triage patients presenting with suspected acute myocardial infarction.

title: Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included. EXPOSURE: Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores. RESULTS: Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

title: AI algorithms and external validation: promises, pitfalls, and a practical blueprint.
abstract: External validation involving the testing of a frozen AI model on independent data from other sites, populations, time periods, or devices provides the clearest estimate of intended-use setting performance when those external data are deployment-representative of the expected population, measurement processes, and clinical workflow. It yields realistic estimates of discrimination and calibration, exposes shortcut learning and distribution shift, quantifies clinical utility through decision-analytic measures, and reveals subgroup disparities requiring mitigation. Yet common pitfalls undermine credibility: quasi-external splits with hidden relatedness; spectrum and prevalence mismatch; site, workflow, and hardware effects; label noise and reference-standard drift; analytic flexibility and selective reporting; small, underpowered samples; reliance only on the area under the curve; unreported threshold tuning; and leakage. A practical blueprint emphasizes pre-registration; representative, multi-site cohorts spanning geography, time, and acquisition; prevention of patient and temporal overlap; comprehensive evaluation of discrimination, calibration (including calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, and calibration plots), and net benefit with confidence intervals; pre-specified subgroup and fairness audits; transparent labelling procedures and uncertainty analyses; principled sample-size calculations; and minimal, well-documented model updating (recalibration before revision). Finally, external validation should connect to post-deployment governance via drift detection, performance triggers, and change-control plans, complemented by site-specific local evaluation to ensure safety and reliability across diverse clinical environments. When executed to these standards, external validation transforms promising prototypes into dependable clinical tools, clarifying where a model performs, where it fails, and what adaptations are necessary for safe, equitable, and sustainable use. This framework links statistical evaluation to clinical use, model updating, and post-deployment monitoring.

title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate whether GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), compared with DPP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase-4) inhibitors or sulfonylureas, are associated with reduced all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalizations in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. METHODS: PRAISE-HFpEF (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction) was a nationwide multicenter cohort study using a new-user, active-comparator design within the national Veterans Affairs Health System (170 US hospitals). Adults with type 2 diabetes between January 1, 2000 and December 31, 2021, were identified from centralized electronic health records. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 were selected using a validated diagnostic algorithm. Exposure was initiation of a GLP-1RA versus DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2021. The primary outcome was time to all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on the propensity score was used to balanced baseline characteristics. RESULTS: Among 179 288 patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, 1024 GLP-1RA users and 796 DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea users met inclusion criteria. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.64-0.95], P=0.01). Weight loss was modestly greater with GLP-1RAs compared with DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea (-12.9% versus -10.1%). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with obese heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower incidence of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with alternative oral agents.

title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. METHODS: In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). FINDINGS: Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156). INTERPRETATION: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. FUNDING: Swiss National Science Foundation, Swiss Heart Foundation, University Hospital Basel, University of Basel, and Foundation for Cardiovascular Research Basel.

title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages-perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)-to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

title: Healthy Dietary Patterns and Incident Cardiovascular Disease in Cancer Survivors: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of noncancer mortality among cancer survivors. The potential influence of healthy dietary patterns on CVD risk among cancer survivors remains poorly understood. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to investigate the association between healthy dietary patterns and incident CVD among cancer survivors. METHODS: We analyzed data from 8,716 cancer survivors initially free of CVD in the UK Biobank cohort. We used 24-hour dietary recall data to calculate 8 dietary pattern scores. Cox proportional hazards models and Fine-Gray competing risks models were used to investigate the association between dietary patterns and incident CVD. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 12.3 (Q1-Q3: 11.6-13.0) years, 1,116 individuals experienced incident CVD events. When comparing the top quintile with the bottom quintile, HRs (95% CI) for total CVD were 0.72 (0.58-0.88) for Mediterranean diet score, 0.74 (0.61-0.89) for Mediterranean-Dietary Approaches to stop Hypertension Diet Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay score, 0.63 (0.52-0.76) for Alternate Healthy Eating Index-2010, 0.65 (0.53-0.79) for Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension score, 0.82 (0.68-0.99) for healthful Plant-Based Diet Index, 0.67 (0.55-0.80) for reversed energy-adjusted diet inflammatory index, and 0.80 (0.67-0.96) for healthy low-fat diet score. The findings remain robust after fitting the generalized propensity score model. At age 45, participants with the highest adherence to healthy dietary patterns gained an estimated life expectancy of 1.66 to 3.32 years more than those with the lowest adherence. CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to healthy dietary patterns is associated with reduced CVD risk among cancer survivors, underscoring the potential for diet to support cardio-oncology care.

title: Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization. OBJECTIVES: The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies. METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P < 0.001) and AFS (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.50-2.86; P < 0.001). For AFS, the excess risk of Rutherford 6 was greatest in the first 3 months (HR: 14.13; 95% CI: 4.94-40.38 vs Rutherford 4; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

title: KLHL3-Cab39 Disruption Drives WNK4-Independent Hyperkalemic Hypertension.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Familial hyperkalemic hypertension, also known as pseudohypoaldosteronism type II (PHAII), is characterized by hypertension and hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis and involves dysregulation of the KLHL3 (Kelch-like 3)-cullin3 E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, affecting WNK1/4 (with-no-lysine kinase 1/4)-mediated SPAK (Ste20-related proline/alanine-rich kinase)/OSR1 (oxidative stress response kinase 1)-NCC (Na+-Cl- cotransporter) signaling. How KLHL3 phosphorylation mutations modulate this pathway remains poorly defined. METHODS: We generated knock-in mouse models expressing phosphomimetic (S486D) or phosphodefective (S486G) mutations at Klhl3 S486 (homologous to human S433). Blood pressure, serum and urine biochemistries, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, coimmunoprecipitation, in vitro ubiquitination assays, and molecular docking were performed. Klhl3 S486G mice were crossed with Wnk4-/- mice to test WNK4 dependence. RESULTS: Both knock-in strains exhibited typical PHAII features despite unchanged KLHL3 levels, with enhanced SPAK/OSR1-NCC phosphorylation, increased Cab39 levels, and unchanged WNK1/4 expression. Under high-salt loading, Klhl3 S486 knock-in mice maintained severe PHAII phenotypes, with persistently elevated Cab39 and NCC levels despite decreased WNK4 expression. Critically, Wnk4 deletion failed to rescue PHAII phenotypes in Klhl3 S486G mice, demonstrating that Klhl3 S486 mutations drive PHAII independently of WNK4. In vitro, human KLHL3 S433D/S433G mutations reduced KLHL3-Cab39 association and Cab39 ubiquitination, with a corresponding increase in Cab39 abundance. Deletion mapping identified KLHL3 residues 428 to 437 and Cab39 residues 314 to 324 as key determinants of the KLHL3-Cab39 association. CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that the integrity of Ser486 itself, rather than its phosphorylation state, is required for KLHL3-mediated Cab39 ubiquitination and define a WNK4-independent PHAII mechanism driven by impaired Cab39 degradation and consequent SPAK/OSR1-Na+-Cl- cotransporter activation.

title: Sudden Cardiac Death in Firefighters From the United States: A 16-Year Postmortem Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is the leading cause of duty-related death among firefighters. Understanding postmortem cardiovascular abnormalities associated with SCD is critical to guiding fire service cardiovascular disease screening and prevention programs. METHODS: This study included US firefighters who had a duty-related death over a 16-year period (1999-2014) with available postmortem reports (autopsy/medical examiner reports). Cases were systematically reviewed to identify cases of SCD. For each SCD case, the primary etiology of SCD was adjudicated by experts in sports cardiology and cardiovascular pathology. RESULTS: Postmortem evaluations were available for 794 of 2100 (37.8%) on-duty firefighter deaths over the study period (average age, 44±13 years; age range, 17-82 years; 4.0% women). A total of 312 of 794 (39.3%) firefighter deaths were adjudicated as SCD. A total of 255 of 312 (81.8%) SCD events were attributable to coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease or hypertensive heart disease, which both are associated with traditional cardiovascular risk factors. The leading etiology of SCD among young firefighters (aged <40 years) was also coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease (24/50 [48.0%]). Of firefighters who had an exertional SCD event thought to be secondary to coronary artery disease (n=97), a total of 62 of 91 (68.1%) had severe fixed coronary stenosis, while 29 of 91 (31.9%) demonstrated acute plaque rupture/thrombosis. CONCLUSIONS: More than 80% of on-duty SCD events among US firefighters are due to coronary artery disease and hypertensive heart disease that may be prevented by early disease identification and risk factor modification. Future studies should assess the efficacy of more rigorous firefighter cardiovascular disease screening and management practices.

title: Salt-Sensitive Hypertension Begins With Intracellular K+ and Water Loss.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Na+ and water overload due to inappropriately low renal salt and water excretion is considered the root cause of salt-sensitive hypertension. However, experimental renal and psoriasis hypertension are characterized by chronic predisposition to dehydration. We tested the validity of this alternative hypertension due to loss of water theory in deoxycorticosterone acetate (DOCA) salt-sensitive hypertension. METHODS: We tested the effect of DOCA (25 mg pellet) in mice on a low Na+ diet (0.02%-0.03%) with tap water, or with Na+ in their drinking water (1% NaCl or 1.44% NaHCO3), on body Na+, K+, and water content 2, 6, and 12 days after treatment initiation.
